title: Intermittent policy-suppression bug causing gradual request suppression across multi-mode deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments reported progressive request suppression (clients receiving throttled responses despite available capacity). Unlike a hard 429 spike, this appeared as gradual suppression over minutes for long-running flows. Initial triage showed rate-control decisions diverging between proxy and orchestrator when policy evaluation windows overlapped during rapid policy changes and autoscaling events.
root_cause: A race in the policy evaluation path: when a policy update (rate/weight changes) lands during an in-flight reconciliation, the local admission adaptor falls back to a stale suppression score. The adaptor then applies a per-route suppression multiplier from the old policy but uses a new epoch for accounting, producing artificially reduced allowed-rate for that tenant. This is compounded by the orchestrator not invalidating short-lived local caches on config rollouts, so some nodes serve with mixed policy state for several minutes.
impact: Multiple mid-market and enterprise customers experienced degraded throughput for sustained jobs and interactive sessions. Observed symptoms: elevated tail latency, gradual increase in soft-rejections (early EOF or small-chunk responses), and tokenized request pacing that appeared as client-side backoff. Several customers opened urgent support tickets; two escalated to account management with business impact reported.
repro_steps: 1) Deploy a policy change (rate increase + new per-route weight) to a multi-region dedicated pool
2) Trigger a burst of long-lived chat sessions and sustained embedding jobs routed via the proxy
3) During autoscale events (new nodes join), concurrently flip the policy via the control plane
4) Observe admission logs: some proxies evaluate using pre-change multipliers while accounting timestamps reflect post-change epochs
5) Metrics show divergence between proxy-accepted rate and orchestrator-expected allowed tokens resulting in progressive suppression on affected nodes
mitigation: Hotfix deployed to proxy adaptor: when policy epoch mismatch detected, fallback to permissive admission (allow) rather than apply stale suppression
Control-plane rollout: serialize policy commits for 30s windows for affected pools to prevent overlapping epochs during autoscale flaps
Manual remediation: for impacted customers we performed a targeted rolling restart of proxies in their pool to flush local caches and restore alignment
